strategy.summary: Reproduce the missing cchg() branch in scipy.special.hyp1f1 for complex z by building the buggy commit dc9cbc03c039 and running the developer's parametrized test_complex_z in scipy/special/tests/test_hypergeometric.py. On the buggy build the a=-0.25, b=0.5, z=1+2j case returns (1+0j) instead of about 1.18-1.28j, so assert_allclose fails. The fixed build restores the cchg line and should pass the non-xfail cases, while the two xfail cases may fail or XPASS without failing the run.

pinned_because: numpy==1.26.4 is the documented reporter environment from issue#20797; numerically_relevant is false, so it is pinned only for era fidelity
scipy is the buggy source revision dc9cbc03c039 built from source, which is the documented 1.13.1-era bug (issue#20797), so no PyPI scipy wheel is used

mkl-dynamic-lp64- has no documented constraint and no era entry; I chose the default OpenBLAS-based numpy wheel and did not install MKL, because hyp1f1's complex path does not call BLAS and the package is not numerically relevant

strategy.reproducing_test: test_complex_z in the parametrized class in scipy/special/tests/test_hypergeometric.py (selected via -k test_complex_z), with the case (-0.25, 0.5, 1+2j, 1.1814553180903435-1.2792130661292984j) as the primary failing parameter
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy dc9cbc03c039, test_complex_z fails on the (-0.25, 0.5, 1+2j) case because hyp1f1 returns (1+0j) and assert_allclose with rtol=4e-15 rejects it; the xfail cases are expected to fail there too. On the fixed revision, the non-xfail parametrizations (-0.25,0.5,1+2j), (0.25,0.5,1+2j), (25,1.5,-2j), (12,-1.5,-10+20j) pass under rtol=4e-15, and the xfail cases may fail or XPASS without making the run fail.
risks: The buggy behaviour is tied to the cchg() complex path in specfun.h; if the buggy revision's build does not compile that path (e.g. a different backend selection), the failure may not reproduce. Verify the buggy build reports (1+0j) before trusting the transition.

The test uses rtol=4e-15, which is tight. Results may differ by libm or CPU (x86_64 vs aarch64, or different FMA usage), so the fixed build could fail the non-xfail cases on other platforms even when the fix is correct. The plan assumes x86_64 Linux.

The MKL dependency name in the environment is truncated and unbounded. Choosing OpenBLAS is an assumption, not evidence; hyp1f1 should not depend on BLAS, but if MKL changes numerics it would not be captured.

The issue text says hyp1f1 is Boost-based, but the root cause is described as a lost line in specfun.h, which is a Fortran-translated routine. The reproduction follows the PR's root-cause account and the test file's references.

The reference value differs in the last digits between the issue (1.1814553180903438-1.2792130661292982j) and the test file (...435-...984j). The test's rtol=4e-15 accepts either, but a stricter check could expose the difference.
The buggy-revision test may also fail on the removed test_cchg_branches path in test_specfun.py if it is run; this plan selects only test_complex_z to keep the transition about the new test.
Building from source requires gfortran and a working meson/ninja toolchain. A build failure would stop the reproduction before any test runs, and that is not evidence about the bug.

oracle.reference_source: mpmath.hyp1f1, checked against Wolfram Alpha Hypergeometric1F1; the 0.1,1,7-24j case was checked with Matlab hypergeom (per the test file comment)
oracle.why: The test compares hyp1f1 against these reference values with assert_allclose at rtol=4e-15; the reference values are stated in the test file and PR context.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy dc9cbc03c039, hyp1f1(-0.25, 0.5, 1+2j) returns (1+0j), which is far from the reference 1.18-1.28j. assert_allclose at rtol=4e-15 raises AssertionError on that parametrization, so test_complex_z fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, the cchg line is restored, so the non-xfail parametrizations (-0.25,0.5,1+2j), (0.25,0.5,1+2j), (25,1.5,-2j), (12,-1.5,-10+20j) should match their references within rtol=4e-15; the xfail cases may fail or XPASS without failing the run.
